chapterNote: Asaph's psalm about the night the comfort stopped working. He cries aloud to God, seeks the Lord in the day of his trouble with his hand stretched out all night and never going numb — and his soul refuses to be comforted. Then a line few would dare write: I remember God, and I groan. Remembering, the standard cure, has become the disease. God holds his eyelids open; he is too disturbed to speak; he goes back over the old days, the years long past, his song in the night, and his spirit searches and searches. Out of that comes the darkest set of questions in the Psalter, six of them: will the Lord reject forever? is His covenant love gone for good? has God forgotten to be gracious, has He in anger shut up His compassion? Then the hinge, in one honest sentence: this is my sickness — and I will remember the years of the right hand of the Most High. He turns the same faculty around and points it the other way, and the psalm changes register entirely. It ends in the poem every Israelite knew: the waters saw You and writhed, the clouds poured, Your arrows flew, Your path was through the sea and Your footprints were not seen. And the last line answers all six questions without arguing: You led Your people like a flock by the hand of Moses and Aaron.

1.text: For the choir director, for Jeduthun. A psalm of Asaph. My voice goes up to God, and I cry out; my voice goes up to God, and He gives ear to me.
1.amp: To the chief Musician [natsach], to Jeduthun, A Psalm [mizmor] of ['for', Asaph, the KJV margin] Asaph [Asaph]. I cried [tsaaq] unto God [Elohim] with my voice [qol], even unto God [Elohim] with my voice [qol]; and He gave ear [azan] unto me.
1.notes: qoli el-Elohim ve-etsaqah (H6963, H430, H6817): my voice to God — and I CRY OUT: tsaaq, the shriek of Israel under Egypt (Exodus 2:23); qoli el-Elohim ve-haazin elai (H238): my voice to God, and He gives ear to me. The line is repeated because the crying was. Jeduthun (H3038) leads the choir here as in Psalm 39, another psalm about not being able to keep quiet.

2.text: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord; by night my hand was stretched out and never went numb; my soul refused to be comforted.
2.amp: In the day [yom] of my trouble [tsarah] I sought [darash] the Lord [Adonai]: my sore ['hand', yad, the KJV margin] ran in the night [layil], and ceased not: my soul [nephesh] refused to be comforted [nacham].
2.notes: be-yom tsarati Adonai darashti (H3117, H6869, H136, H1875): in the day of my distress I SOUGHT the Lord. yadi lailah niggerah ve-lo taphug (H3027, H3915, H5064, H6313): my HAND — the margin's literal, where the KJV text reads 'sore' — was stretched out in the night and did not go numb: the prayer-posture held till dawn. meanah hinnachem naphshi (H3985, H5315): my soul REFUSED to be comforted — Jacob's refusal over Joseph (Genesis 37:35). Sought God all night, and would not be consoled: both true at once.

3.text: I remember God, and I groan; I complain, and my spirit grows faint. Selah.
3.amp: I remembered [zakar] God [Elohim], and was troubled [hamah]: I complained [siach], and my spirit [ruach] was overwhelmed [ataph]. Selah [Selah].
3.notes: ezkerah Elohim ve-ehemayah (H2142, H430, H1993): I REMEMBER God — and I groan: hamah, the roar of a troubled sea; asichah ve-titateph ruchi (H7878, H5848): I complain, and my spirit FAINTS — ataph, the wrapping-weakness of Psalm 61:2. The most unsettling line in the psalm: remembering God, which every other psalm prescribes as the cure, is here the thing that hurts. Selah.

4.text: You hold my eyelids open; I am too disturbed to speak.
4.amp: You hold [achaz] mine eyes [ayin] waking: I am so troubled [paam] that I cannot speak [dabar].
4.notes: achazta shemurot enai (H270, H5869, H8109): You have GRIPPED the watches of my eyes — the eyelids held apart, insomnia attributed directly to God; nipamti ve-lo adabber (H6470, H1696): I am beaten — paam, to strike, the verb behind a footfall and a pulse — and I cannot speak. The one who cried aloud in verse 1 has lost the power of speech by verse 4.

5.text: I have thought over the days of old, the years long past.
5.amp: I have considered [chashab] the days [yom] of old [qedem], the years [shanah] of ancient times [olam].
5.notes: chishshavti yamim mi-qedem (H2803, H3117, H6924): I have RECKONED UP days from of old — chashab, the accountant's verb; shenot olamim (H8141, H5769): the years of ages past. He goes to the archives, which is the right instinct; verses 7-9 show what he finds there when the light is bad.

6.text: At night I remember my song; I muse with my own heart, and my spirit searches:
6.amp: I call to remembrance [zakar] my song [neginah] in the night [layil]: I commune [siach] with mine own heart [lebab]: and my spirit [ruach] made diligent search [chaphas].
6.notes: ezkerah neginati ba-lailah (H2142, H5058, H3915): I remember my NEGINAH — my music, the song he used to be able to sing in the dark (Job 35:10); im-lebabi asichah va-yechappes ruchi (H3824, H7878, H2664): with my heart I complain, and my spirit SEARCHES — chaphas, to dig through, ransack. Then the six questions.

7.text: 'Will the Lord reject forever? Will He never again show favor?
7.amp: Will the Lord [Adonai] cast off [zanach] for ever [olam]? and will He be favourable [ratsah] no more [yasaph]?
7.notes: ha-le-olamim yiznach Adonai (H5769, H2186, H136): will the Lord REJECT for ages? — zanach, the abandonment-verb of Psalm 44:9 and 88:14; ve-lo-yosiph li-rtsot od (H3254, H7521): and will He not ADD to be favorable again? The first two of six questions, and all six expect the answer no while feeling the answer yes.

8.text: Has His covenant love ended for good? Is His word finished for all generations?
8.amp: Is His mercy [chesed — covenant love] clean gone [aphes] for ever [netsach]? does His promise [omer] fail [gamar] for evermore ['to generation and generation', dor, the KJV margin]?
8.notes: he-apheis la-netsach chasdo (H656, H5331, H2617): has His CHESED come to an end forever — aphes, to cease utterly, the word behind 'there is none else' (Isaiah 45:5); gamar omer le-dor va-dor (H1584, H562, H1755): is His word FINISHED to generation and generation, the margin's literal? The one attribute the whole Old Testament says is permanent (Psalm 136), questioned out loud in Scripture. The Bible lets a believer ask this.

9.text: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has He shut up His compassion in anger?' Selah.
9.amp: Has God [El] forgotten [shakach] to be gracious [chanan]? has He in anger [aph] shut up His tender mercies [rachamim]? Selah [Selah].
9.notes: ha-shakhach channot El (H7911, H2589, H410): has GOD FORGOTTEN how to be gracious? — chanan, the grace-verb of Exodus 34:6; im-qaphats be-aph rachamav (H7092, H639, H7356): or has He in anger SHUT UP His compassions — qaphats, to close a hand or a mouth: the womb-mercy of God imagined clamped shut. The sixth question, and the Selah after it is the silence of a man who has asked everything he can ask.

10.text: And I said, 'This is my sickness: the years of the right hand of the Most High — I will remember them.'
10.amp: And I said [amar], This is my infirmity [chalah]: but I will remember the years [shanah] of the right hand [yamin] of the most High [Elyon].
10.notes: va-omar challoti hi (H559, H2470): and I said, this is my SICKNESS — chalah, to be weak or ill: he diagnoses his own despair rather than defending it; shenot yemin Elyon (H8141, H3225, H5945): the years of the right hand of Elyon. The hinge of the psalm, and the whole turn is one decision: take the faculty that was torturing him in verse 3 — remembering — and aim it at what God's right hand has actually done.

11.text: I will bring to mind the deeds of Yah; yes, I will remember Your wonders from of old.
11.amp: I will remember [zakar] the works of the LORD [Yah]: surely I will remember [zakar] Your wonders [pele] of old [qedem].
11.notes: azkir maalle-Yah (H2142, H4611, H3050): I will bring to REMEMBRANCE the deeds of Yah; ki-ezkerah mi-qedem pilekha (H6924, H6382): for I will remember Your wonder from of old. The verb three times in two verses: the psalm's cure is not a new fact but an old one, deliberately rehearsed.

12.text: I will meditate on all Your work, and murmur over Your deeds.
12.amp: I will meditate [hagah] also of all Your work [poal], and talk [siach] of Your doings [alilot].
12.notes: ve-hagiti be-khol-poolekha (H1897, H6467): I will MURMUR over all Your work — hagah, the same low muttering that Psalm 1:2 does with the law; u-ba-alilotekha asichah (H5949, H7878): and over Your deeds I will muse — siach, the same complaint-verb as verses 3 and 6, now with a different object. Nothing about his practice has changed except what he points it at.

13.text: O God, Your way is in holiness; what god is great like God?
13.amp: Your way [derek], O God [Elohim], is in the sanctuary [qodesh]: who is so great [gadol] a God [El] as our God [Elohim]?
13.notes: Elohim ba-qodesh darkekha (H430, H6944, H1870): God, Your way is in the QODESH — in holiness, or in the sanctuary: both readings are ancient, and verse 19 will answer with a different location for the same road; mi-El gadol k-Elohim (H410, H1419): what god is great like God? Exodus 15:11's question, and the psalm is about to quote the rest of that song.

14.text: You are the God who does wonders; You have made Your strength known among the peoples.
14.amp: You are the God [El] that does [asah] wonders [pele]: You have declared [yada] Your strength [oz] among the people [am].
14.notes: attah ha-El oseh phele (H410, H6213, H6382): YOU are the God who does WONDER — pele, the singular: not a category but a specific act, and verses 16-20 name it; hodata ba-ammim uzzekha (H3045, H5971, H5797): You have MADE KNOWN Your strength among the peoples. The exodus was public, which is why it is usable as evidence.

15.text: With Your arm You redeemed Your people, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
15.amp: You have with Your arm [zeroa] redeemed [gaal] Your people [am], the sons [ben] of Jacob [Yaaqob] and Joseph [Yoseph]. Selah [Selah].
15.notes: gaalta bi-zroa ammekha (H1350, H2220, H5971): You REDEEMED with an arm Your people — gaal, the kinsman-redeemer's verb, Exodus 6:6's word for the exodus; bene-Yaaqob ve-Yoseph (H1121, H3290, H3130): the sons of Jacob and Joseph — Joseph named beside Jacob because Asaph's psalms keep the northern tribes in view (Psalm 78:67; 80:1). Selah, and then the poem.

16.text: The waters saw You, O God; the waters saw You and writhed; the depths themselves shook.
16.amp: The waters [mayim] saw [raah] You, O God [Elohim], the waters [mayim] saw [raah] You; they were afraid [chul — writhed]: the depths [tehom] also were troubled [ragaz].
16.notes: rauka mayim Elohim rauka mayim yachilu (H7200, H4325, H430, H2342): the waters SAW You, God — the waters saw You, they WRITHED — chul, the labor-pain verb; aph yirgezu tehomot (H637, H7264, H8415): indeed the tehomot — the deeps of Genesis 1:2 — shook. Habakkuk 3:10 rewrites this line. The sea does not part; it goes into labor.

17.text: The clouds poured out water; the skies gave out a sound; Your arrows also flew everywhere.
17.amp: The clouds poured out [zaram] water [mayim]: the skies sent out [natan] a sound [qol]: Your arrows also went abroad [halak].
17.notes: zoremu mayim abot (H2229, H4325, H5645): the thick clouds POURED water; qol natenu shechaqim (H6963, H5414, H7834): the skies GAVE a voice; aph-chatsatsekha yithallakhu (H2687): indeed Your arrows went walking — the lightning of Psalm 18:14. A storm at the sea crossing, which Exodus 14:24 hints at and this poem paints.

18.text: Your thunder's voice was in the whirlwind; lightnings lit the world up; the earth shuddered and quaked.
18.amp: The voice [qol] of Your thunder [raam] was in the heaven: the lightnings [baraq] lightened [or] the world [tebel]: the earth [eretz] trembled [ragaz] and shook [raash].
18.notes: qol raamkha ba-galgal (H6963, H7482, H1534): the voice of Your thunder was in the GALGAL — a wheel, hence the whirlwind, which is how the WEB reads it and the KJV takes as 'the heaven'. heiru beraqim tebel (H215, H1300, H8398): lightnings LIT the world. ragezah va-tiras ha-arets (H7264, H7493, H776): the earth trembled and quaked — the line Psalm 97:4 shares.

19.text: Your way was through the sea, and Your path through great waters, and Your footprints were not known.
19.amp: Your way [derek] is in the sea [yam], and Your path in the great [rab] waters [mayim], and Your footsteps [aqeb — heel-prints] are not known [yada].
19.notes: ba-yam darkekha (H3220, H1870): in the SEA was Your way — the answer to verse 13's 'Your way is in holiness': the holy road ran through the water; u-shebilekha be-mayim rabbim (H7635, H7227, H4325): and Your path in many waters; ve-iqqebotekha lo nodau (H6119, H3045): and Your HEEL-PRINTS were not known — the tide erased them. God's route is real and unreadable at once, which is the psalm's whole answer to its six questions: no footprints does not mean no crossing (cf. Romans 11:33).

20.text: Like a flock You led Your people along, by the hand of Moses and of Aaron.
20.amp: You led [nachah] Your people [am] like a flock [tson] by the hand [yad] of Moses [Mosheh] and Aaron [Aharon].
20.notes: nachita kha-tson ammekha (H5148, H6629, H5971): You LED like a flock Your people — nachah, the shepherd-verb of Psalm 23:3; be-yad-Mosheh ve-Aharon (H3027, H4872, H175): by the hand of Moses and Aaron. The psalm ends without going back to the questions of verses 7-9, and without a resolution sentence: the answer is a memory of being shepherded, and two ordinary men's hands are the instrument. The invisible footprints (v. 19) belonged to a Shepherd all along.
